newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns Zaire air raids.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns Zaire air raids.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday condemned Zairean government air raids on rebel-held centres and other acts of violence in eastern Zaire, saying they would only drag out the conflict in the region.
At least 19 people were reported killed in Monday's raids, and thousands of residents were fleeing the area on Tuesday.
"The United States condemns the recent escalation of violence in eastern Zaire, including the air attacks on Bukavu, Walekale and Shabunda," said State Department spokesman Glyn Davies.
"Such acts serve only to perpetuate the conflict and encourage further violence," Davies told a news briefing.
"We call again on all parties to refrain from violence and begin immediately a direct dialogue aimed at achieving a peaceful settlement to this conflict."

Monday's was the first air raid confirmed independently since Tutsi-led rebels began a military campaign last October, seizing a swath of eastern Zaire some 600 miles (1,000 km) long bordering on Rwanda, Uganda, Burundi and Tanzania.
